summary: The finite quantum budget separates logical reads from physical bit queries and proves a uniform log-sixth-power bound with very loose constants depending only on k. The sequential-continuation proof correctly explains the formal output-interface variant without changing the preceding ordinary algorithm. The classical section starts with a four-step planting overview, then proves a separate-cap direct product via transcript rectangles and optimal posterior continuation values. The adaptive cap-event example is especially useful: its explicit5/16 joint and5/8 conditional successes show why conditioning on nonheaviness cannot be used. The optional weighted proof handles zero-mass branches without posteriors and is linked algebraically to the first proof. The finite minimax construction then obtains a promised-support hard law with a strict common margin, after P and L are fixed; it is explicitly different from the Gaussian interpolation law.
